## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `263527d3d538f2ef4d39cb94ecfd57f49c4d4857`
Local-runs: none
Scope: AGENTS.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml, .github/workflows/upgrade-harness-optin.yml + scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs, scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs, scripts/pm/check-expected-skips.mjs, scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs, scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs, docs/agents/multi-agent-discipline.md, scripts/check-shard-attestation.mjs (judge, the dogfood fixtures, the cancel-cause prefixes), scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs, .github/workflows/lint.yml (job-to-gate map), scripts/check-partof-closing-keyword.mjs (RULE 1 and RULE 3, for the `Part of` line), precedent #25867 (an issue; landed by #25881, `487056b940`), precedent #26460 (`Test UI`, cited by the follow-up ruling), the live ruleset for `main`

Round 2 of this review. Round 1 gave PASS on `4bb48774cf` with three wording should-fixes S1–S3 and one escalation (the required-set question). Since then the maintainer ruled that question (6669982756, A in two steps), the seat pushed one commit `263527d3d5`, and the PR body changed `Fixes #30461` to `Part of #30461`. This record supersedes round 1 for this head; the round-1 judgments are restated where they still hold and changed where they do not.

Inputs read: card #30461 body and its five comments (ruling 6663883327, seat note 6664079672, claim 6666075446, dev report 6667658973, follow-up ruling 6669982756); PR #30639 body as of 2026-11-05T21:45:50Z and its file list; the net diff `origin/main...263527d3d5` (merge-base `63de248a1c`, 10 files, +206/-77) and the round-2 delta `4bb48774cf..263527d3d5` (3 files, +13/-8); the head's check-runs; `rules/branches/main`. The tree was judged, not the body's account of it.

**The round-2 delta** (`263527d3d5`, "docs(ci): the queue-build dogfood red is advisory, and the stale wall-time figure is the measured median") touches three files and no executable text: the ci.yml hunk sits inside the `#` THE TWO SPEEDS block (hunk 122–130; the block opens at 116 and every line of it starts with `#`), the check-required-contexts.mjs hunk inside the `/** … */` tombstone that closes at line 395 above `export const REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` at 396 (hunk 384–397; every changed line starts with ` * `), and the discipline-doc hunk is prose. No `if:`, no filter output, no regex, no fixture and no self-test changed, so every ① derived judgment of round 1 is a judgment of this head as well; they are restated below unchanged.

**Check-runs on the head** (read 2026-11-05T21:53:37Z, eight minutes after the push at 21:45:44Z; the set is NOT yet complete): 59 check-runs listed — 26 `success`, 8 `skipped`, 0 `failure`/`cancelled`/`timed_out`, 25 `in_progress`. Every gate family this review derives from had completed and is `success`: `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (check:shard-attestation, check:required-contexts, check:ci-filter-parity, scheduled-full-run --self-test and --check-concurrency), `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (check:pm-expected-skips, check:pm-skill-ratchet), `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (check:pm-dispatch-gates), `Lint · ESLint`, the three `Lint · scoped ·` jobs, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`. `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success` with `Dogfood Regression Gate (${{ matrix.shard }}/3)` and `Dogfood Verify CLI` both `skipped` — the pull_request shape ① predicts, unchanged by a comments-only delta. `Check Changeset` is `skipped` on this head (round 1 read it `success` on `4bb48774cf`); the delta touches no package path, so a skip is the filter's answer, not a red. Still `in_progress` at the read: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8)`, the sixteen `Test UI (n/16)` shards, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` — the build/test half of the required set, on a diff that changed one YAML comment block, one JSDoc block and one Markdown paragraph. The seat owes the completed read at merge time; this record's PASS is conditional on none of those going red, which nothing in the delta can cause. Combined commit status is `pending` with zero statuses set, i.e. no status context exists; not a gate.

**Live ruleset** (`rules/branches/main`, re-read 2026-11-05T21:47Z): the same ten required contexts as round 1 — `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`. `Dogfood Regression Gate` is NOT in the set, which is exactly what the follow-up ruling's step 1 ("⛔ No ruleset change in it") requires of this PR.

**The three round-1 should-fixes against the delta:**

- **S1 — closed.** ci.yml now reads "so a dogfood red shows on the queue build of the entry that carries it rather than first on `main`'s push run after it. It is advisory there: the context is outside the required set (below), so the queue may merge the entry before or despite the shards." The ordering promise ("before the merge") is gone; "rather than first on" is true (the queue build is the first run that carries the shards on that change); "(below)" resolves to the block's own sentence "The queue enforces only the ruleset's required set, and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is outside it since #22998" at line 142, fifteen lines down in the same block; "before or despite the shards" is the correct statement of an advisory context under `ALLGREEN` on the required set only. The discipline doc now reads "so a dogfood red shows on the queue build, advisory only". Both true against the ruleset read today.
- **S2 — closed.** The tombstone's "the instruction files name them correctly as full-battery jobs" became "the instruction files name where each runs", which is true of both names: AGENTS.md:513–514 and the discipline paragraph name the shards on queue runs and `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` in the full battery. The appended paragraph adds "`Temporal Conformance` stays full-battery only" (true: `temporal-conformance` keeps both exclusions at head) and states the follow-up path: "the follow-up ruling on #30461 (A, in two steps, 6669982756) puts it back only after a clean 24-hour reading of the queue builds, the row here landing first and the ruleset edit after it". Checked clause by clause against 6669982756 items 2–3: the reading is 24 h after landing, the gate is the threshold in item 3, the `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` row "merges first, before the ruleset edit". True.
- **S3 — closed on substance, in the lesser of the two forms offered.** The figure is updated: "about 20 minutes of wall per queue entry (median, 2026-11-05)" against the PR's own 20.4 min (`success`) / 20.5 min (all conclusions) median. The first clause still reads "PR and queue runs carry the fast set" rather than the AGENTS.md spelling ("PR runs carry the fast set, queue runs add the dogfood shards"); it is not false — queue runs do carry the fast set, and the paragraph's fourth sentence adds the shards — so the paragraph as a whole is true, and the "10 minutes" contradiction that S3 was about is gone. Two precision notes, not findings: the quantity behind "wall per queue entry" is CI run duration on `merge_group` (`updated_at − run_started_at`), not queue residence, and the date stamp correctly marks it as the before-reading, so the 24 h after-reading should refresh it.

**`Part of #30461`.** Right, and `Fixes` would now be wrong: the follow-up ruling says in terms "The card therefore stays open after #30639 merges, until the step-3 report and the `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` row land, or step 3 stops at a flake fix", and GitHub closes a `Fixes #N` target on merge whatever the surrounding prose says (the defect `check:partof-closing-keyword` exists to block). The body's `Part of` line carries no closing keyword for #30461 anywhere else (RULE 1), and the parenthetical that follows it reads as not closing, with no keyword bound inside it (RULE 3); `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` is `success` on this head. The parenthetical's account of why ("the follow-up ruling 6669982756 owes a 24-hour reading of the queue builds after this lands, then the required-set step") is true.

### ① Derived judgments

Unchanged from round 1; the delta is comments and prose only (verified above), so each was re-read against the head rather than re-derived.

1. **Which events run the three shards.** `dogfood`'s `if:` at head is `!cancelled() && needs.filter.outputs.core != 'false' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'`. So: `push` to `main` (when the push diff sets `core`, as before), `schedule`, `workflow_dispatch`, and now `merge_group`. `pull_request` stays denied. `dogfood-verify`, `temporal-conformance` and `ui-published-artifacts` keep both exclusions. **Right**, and exactly letter B: one conjunct removed from one job.
2. **`filter.outputs.core` on `merge_group`.** `core: ${{ github.event_name != 'merge_group' && steps.changes.outputs.core || 'true' }}` — on `merge_group` the guard is false, `false && x` is false, `false || 'true'` is `'true'`. The `filter` job has no `if:`, so it runs on every event. If `filter` itself fails (checkout flake, timeout; the dorny step is `continue-on-error` on `merge_group`), its outputs are empty and `'' != 'false'` is true, so the shards run (THE FILTER CONTRACT half 2, fail-open). The PR's claim "the shards cannot skip silently there" is **right**: the only skip path on a queue build is a run-level cancellation.
3. **`dogfood-gate` (`if: always()`) on a queue build** with the shards run and `dogfood-verify` skipped: `judge()` takes `--leg dogfood/3:success` (roster required, three credentials present) and `--leg dogfood-verify/1:skipped` with `filterResult === 'success'` → "satisfied (skipped by the filter — #4928; expected attestations: 0)"; expected 3, present 3, **green**. Pinned by the existing self-test "dogfood: each leg is judged on its own roster — a full matrix + a filter-skipped CLI leg ⇒ green". A failing shard reads `failure` on the leg → red; a shard that never attests → "MISSING" → red. **Right.** On a PR: both legs skipped, filter success → expected 0, green (observed on this head). On a filter-skipped diff (a `push` whose diff sets `core=false`): both legs skipped → expected 0, green. On `merge_group` a filter-skipped diff cannot arise for `core` (always `'true'`). This is also the third item the follow-up ruling asks the 24 h reading to confirm ("counts 3 credentials and judges `Dogfood Verify CLI` as skipped"): the code says it will, and the reading is the live proof. The ruling's step-4 fuse ("revert #30639 … brings the gate back to zero expected credentials and `success`") is likewise what the judge does when both legs skip on a queue build.
4. **`jobIfReading` / `notOnPullRequest` (dispatch-gates).** The queue clause regex `/\s*&&\s*github\.event_name\s*!=\s*'pull_request'\s*$/` is applied only when the full-battery clause did not match, as the last conjunct. Traced: `A && != 'pull_request'` reads refs + `notOnPullRequest: true`, `fullBatteryOnly: false`; `A && != 'merge_group' && != 'pull_request'` (reordered) strips the trailing clause, leaves `!= 'merge_group'`, fails the output term → null (refused, as the test says); `A && != 'pull_request' && != 'pull_request'` → one left over → null; the clause in front of the output → null; `(A || B) && != 'pull_request'` → reads. The full-battery row now also carries `notOnPullRequest: true`, and `fullBatteryOnlyClause` checks `fullBatteryOnly` first, so Dogfood Verify CLI's sentence is unchanged. **Right.** Without this change the shards' row would have DROPPED from `--commands` (the old `if:` was readable, the new one was the refused "one event alone" case), so the fix was owed by the ci.yml change itself.
5. **Does any OTHER job's reading change?** Every job-level `if:` across `.github/workflows/*.yml` at head was listed: the only one ending in a lone `!= 'pull_request'` is `dogfood`'s. The other lone exclusions (fleet-patrols, governed-surface-guard, shard-timings-refresh, ui-test-timings-refresh, validate-deps, checklist-status) are STEP-level, which neither `jobIfReading` (reads `extractJobBlocks`' job-level `if:`) nor check-expected-skips' `jobGate(job.if)` reads. **No other job's reading changes.** Right.
6. **Expected-skips reason.** `pr-event` terms merge into one `events` list; "full battery only" is now said only when `PR_EVENTS.every(...)`; the shards keep their derived row (a PR head still skips them, which is what the roster verifies) with the reason "skips on every PR head and is answered by the merge-queue build and main's push and scheduled runs". The fixture tree models the new live shape. **Right.**
7. **Cited and left alone, verified in the code:** `check-shard-attestation.mjs` reads no `event_name` anywhere outside fixtures and pins only `if: always()` on the gates; its cancel-cause classifier is prefix-based (`'Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for'`), so a `merge_group` concurrency group is classified the same as a `pull_request` one. `check-required-contexts.mjs` pins registry rows only; `Dogfood Regression Gate` is not one, and the delta edits its tombstone comment, not a row. `check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` reads filter globs; no `event_name` in it. `release.yml`'s `full-battery` and `scheduled-full-run.mjs --release-gate` read `schedule`/`push` runs only, which is still the right source since `dogfood-verify` and the temporal leg stay off the queue. All **right**.
8. **Now-live dormant code.** The `dogfood` build step's `TURBO_CACHE: … merge_group … 'local:rw,remote:rw'` was dead under the old deny-list and is live now; the identical expression appears 8 times in ci.yml, on jobs that already run on `merge_group`, so it is the established queue policy, and the local turbo seed save stays `push`-only. Not a finding.
9. **No gate pins the edited prose.** Swept `scripts/` and `.github/` at head for pins on the THE TWO SPEEDS wording ("before the merge", "rather than on `main`"), the tombstone sentence and the discipline doc's path: `dispatch-gates.mjs:1184` and `check-expected-skips.mjs:371` name the block, neither quotes its sentences; nothing under `scripts/` reads `docs/agents/multi-agent-discipline.md`; the 120-byte line ratchet (`check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`) covers AGENTS.md and the agent files, not `docs/agents/`, and AGENTS.md is untouched by the delta (its two Two speeds lines stay 117 B / 118 B). So the delta can move no gate; the check-runs confirm it.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged. No published package, schema or `.changeset` is touched: a workflow (Tier H), four PM/CI scripts with their self-tests, and prose; the delta adds only comments. `skip-changeset` is right and `Clause-②: no` (plain, not `(narrowing)`) is the right line: nothing a consumer declared is taken away. The face is **rules** (governed paths `.github/workflows/**`, `AGENTS.md`) ⇒ CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, which is what this record serves. Semver level: **none**.

### ③ Boundary flags

**(a) "ejects the PR from the queue" vs the required set — now ruled; the round-1 escalation closes.** Round 1 found that ruling 6663883327's binding text rested on the card body's "Facts" calling `Dogfood Regression Gate` "the required context" (false since #22998), so that this PR alone makes a dogfood red visible on the queue build but does not eject the entry, and asked the seat to raise the required-set question. The follow-up ruling 6669982756 (maintainer 「同意」 2026-11-05T21:25Z) states the same gap in its own words ("PR #30639 alone makes a dogfood red visible on the queue build but does not eject the entry") and binds A in two steps: (1) this PR lands under letter B with no ruleset change; (2) the owed 24 h after-reading gains three items — entries that ran dogfood and whether the shards ran, each red classed (a) own regression / (b) flake / (c) inherited, and the 3-credentials-plus-skipped-CLI confirmation; (3) threshold — at most one (b), no environmental failure, queue median wall-time increase ≤ 2 min — then the maintainer adds the context to the ruleset after a `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` row lands first as an XS PR; (4) a fuse — if once required flakes eject ≥ 3 entries in a day the lane may revert #30639. The tree at this head is consistent with every one of those: no ruleset or registry row is touched (step 1); the gate's queue-build judgment matches item 2's third bullet (①3); the fuse's mechanism is what the judge does under the old deny list (①3). The prose that round 1 asked to stop overstating now states the advisory limit in all three places (S1, S2). The two rulings do not conflict: 6663883327 binds the code change (letter B, one conjunct) and 6669982756 binds what follows it; the seat's reading in the PR body's Acceptance notes says exactly this. **No escalation remains open from this review.** What is owed next is the seat's, not the PR's: the 24 h reading in the ruled shape.

**(b) `AGENTS.md` and `docs/agents/multi-agent-discipline.md`, outside the claim's file surface.** Necessary restatement, not overreach (unchanged from round 1): AGENTS.md's Two speeds line literally said "PR and queue runs carry the fast set", which the tree now contradicts, and the claim's surface already named "every comment that restates the dogfood deny list". Truth of the lines at this head: AGENTS.md:513–514 ("PR runs carry the fast set, queue runs add the dogfood shards; `main`'s scheduled and push runs carry the full battery") — **true**, 117 B and 118 B inside the 120 B budget. Discipline paragraph: the shards on queue runs, "advisory only", the three legs staying full-battery only, "the context is outside the required set, so the queue does not hold an entry on it", and "about 20 minutes of wall per queue entry (median, 2026-11-05)" — all **true** against the tree, the ruleset and the PR's own measurement. The round-1 overstatement is gone.

**(c) The before-reading of queue wall time, now with a ruled threshold.** The before figure (`actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?event=merge_group&created=` at-or-after `2026-11-04T18:41:25Z`, pages 1–4, `duration = updated_at − run_started_at`, completed runs, `run_attempt 1`; n=303, median 20.5 min all conclusions, 20.4 min `success`) is sound as a like-for-like comparand. The follow-up ruling's item 3 now hangs a decision on it: "a queue median wall-time increase of at most 2 minutes". For that threshold to be meaningful the after-reading must (i) use the same formula, filters (completed, `run_attempt 1`), event and a 24 h window, and compare the same conclusion class (the body gives both; `success`-only, n=285, 20.4 min, is the steadier of the two); (ii) be named as CI run duration on `merge_group`, not queue residence (enqueue → merge, which includes waiting for a build slot and for entries ahead) — `run_started_at` excludes pre-start pickup wait, so a slower runner pickup under +3 jobs per entry would show as in-run job pickup (captured) rather than run start (not); (iii) carry the discipline doc's "about 20 minutes" forward if it moves. The critical-path reading (60 newest `success` runs; `Test Core` closes 38/60 at median 20.8 min) and the push-side shard timing (11.4 min median, 12.3 p90, 14.2 max) remain the right comparands for "should move little". Fine as the before half; the after half is the seat's.

### ④ Design judgment

Held against ruling 6663883327 (letter B), the follow-up 6669982756 (A in two steps) and the code they cite: `merge_group` alone leaves the deny list; `pull_request` stays denied; `dogfood-verify`, `temporal-conformance` and `ui-published-artifacts` keep both exclusions; no affected-only filter (the shards ride `core`, which is `'true'` on every queue entry); no ruleset or registry change. Precedent #25867/#25881 is the same shape one layer down (the filter's ui outputs reading the queue diff) and this PR correctly does NOT copy it onto `core` (that would be letter C). Precedent #26460 (`Test UI`, cited by the follow-up ruling) is the same question for another context and was answered the same way — ruling 6435318516, letter A staged: a flake reading on `main` first (6436579765, "no Test UI flake is live"), then the aggregate enrolled in `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` and the ruleset — which is the shape the two-step path copies. Attempts to break it (round 1, re-read at head):

- `filter` skipped or failed on a queue build: `filter` has no `if:`, so it skips only under run cancellation (`!cancelled()` then skips the shards; the gate reads `filterResult === 'cancelled'` → satisfied). A failed `filter` runs the shards fail-open and reds the gate on the skipped verify leg ("skipped while the filter job did not succeed") — the same red the old tree produced, so no new direction. Advisory either way.
- `!cancelled()` semantics: untouched in position and in both readers' stripping.
- Attestation counting on a queue build: 3 of 3 + 0 expected; a credential from the skipped leg would red the gate (pinned), a missing or failed shard reds it. The `--leg dogfood/3` roster, `fail-fast: false` and the credential steps without `if:` are unchanged.
- A later trigger added to `on:`: the deny-list spelling runs the shards on it, and the dorny allow-list leaves `core` as `'true'` there — the failure direction is a slower run, never a silent skip, as the header says.
- The revert fuse (follow-up ruling step 4): restoring `&& github.event_name != 'merge_group'` puts both legs back to skipped on a queue build → expected 0 → `success`, with `jobIfReading` reading the restored spelling as full-battery (the pre-PR path, still pinned by the LIVE pin on `Dogfood Verify CLI`). The revert is one conjunct and needs no ruleset step, as the ruling says.
- Prose vs tree: swept `.github`, `scripts`, `docs`, `*.md`, skills at head for the old deny-list prose and for "fast set"/"full battery"/"before the merge" restatements; every remaining statement is updated or still true. `upgrade-harness-optin.yml`'s sentence is true: the harness test lives under `packages/qa/dogfood/test/`, so its first R2 answer is now the queue build.

Findings:

- **S1, S2, S3 (round 1) — closed** in `263527d3d5`, as judged above.
- **S4 (should-fix, PR body only, not the tree):** the body's 维护者速读 is now stale against the follow-up ruling in two places, while the body's own Acceptance notes are current. 「为什么改」 ends "现在 dogfood 红会出现在该条目的队列构建上，合并之前就能看到" — the "before the merge" ordering that S1 removed from the tree; and 「风险与回滚」 ends "要不要把它加回必需集合，裁决没定，席位另行呈报" — the required-set question is now ruled (6669982756, A in two steps), and the seat has already reported. The 速读 is the Tier H approver's first read, so it should say what the Acceptance notes say: 队列里的 dogfood 红是提示性的（不在必需集合，队列可能先合并）；加回必需集合已由后续裁决 6669982756 定为两步（先 24 小时读数，再 `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` 行，后改 ruleset）. Wording only; the squash message is taken from the body, so it is worth fixing before the merge.
- **Notes, not this card's (pre-existing, unchanged by this PR):** the `dogfood` job's `timeout-minutes: 30` comment still says "~6× a shard (~5 min)" against the PR's own 11.4 min median / 14.2 max (the 30-minute backstop still holds at about 2× the max). The tombstone's first paragraph still says "their legs run in the FULL BATTERY only — `main`'s push, hourly and dispatch runs": "hourly" predates the 4-hourly cadence, and the present tense is now amended, not replaced, by the "Since #30461" paragraph beneath it; both are readable as the #22998 account and the second paragraph carries the current state.
- Must-fix: **none.** The `if:` change is the one ruled conjunct, the delta adds no executable text, every derived gate that had completed on the head is green and the pending ones are named above, the two readers that would otherwise have misdescribed the new spelling are corrected with LIVE pins and ablations, the ruled effect's limit is stated in the tree in the follow-up ruling's own terms, and the body's `Part of` keeps the card open as that ruling requires.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-30461-dogfood-merge-group`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:devx#2` · Head-sha `263527d3d538f2ef4d39cb94ecfd57f49c4d4857` · 2026-11-05T22:05Z

- **Shape:** 10 files, +206/−77, read from the diff and not the report. The behaviour change is a single conjunct: the `dogfood` job's `if:` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` drops `github.event_name != 'merge_group'` and keeps `!cancelled()`, the `core` filter and `!= 'pull_request'`. `dogfood-verify`, `temporal-conformance` and `ui-published-artifacts` are unchanged. The rest is prose that restates the split (THE TWO SPEEDS, release.yml, upgrade-harness-optin.yml, `AGENTS.md`, the discipline doc and the required-contexts tombstone) and the two readers of a job's `if:`. `dispatch-gates.mjs` gains a `notOnPullRequest` reading with LIVE pins and an ablation. `check-expected-skips.mjs` calls a job "full battery only" only when both events are excluded.
- **Rulings:** letter B (6663883327) and the follow-up A in two steps (6669982756). The tree matches both. There is no ruleset or `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` change, and the text says the queue-build red is advisory until the context rejoins the required set. The PR body says `Part of #30461`, so the card stays open for the after-reading.
- **Contract review:** PASS in two rounds, record 6670580911 on this head. Round 1, on `4bb48774cf`, raised three wording should-fixes. The seat closed them in `263527d3d5`. The review's S4, the stale 维护者速读 in the PR body, is fixed by a body patch. Must-fix: none.
- **Gates:**
  - Head checks: 56 `success` and 11 skipped, none red, mergeable clean.
  - `check-expected-skips`: OK, all 11 skips are in main's roster (exit 0).
  - `check-governed-merges`: GOVERNED, 4 of 10 paths on the register (ci.yml, release.yml, upgrade-harness-optin.yml and `AGENTS.md`), landing tier H. 283 changed lines, which is ≤ 3000.
  - The seat ran `dispatch-gates --commands` on this head: 80 of 80 exit 0, and `--ran` reconciled (80 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED).
- **Before-reading:** the PR body records queue wall time on `merge_group` CI runs over the 24 hours before the change, with the queries: 303 runs, median 20.5 min, p90 26.0 min.
- **Owed after landing:** the 24-hour reading on #30461 that ruling 6669982756 step 2 lists. Its threshold decides the required-set step.
- **Out of scope:** `Skills-docs:` n/a, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Landing:** Tier H. Ready, reviewers os-zhuang and hotlong, `needs-user-decision`. The seat lands it after an authorized APPROVED review.
